  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:

          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'

        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

## Summary

I implemented telephone normalization on owner creation so the app satisfies the spec and all tests pass (`Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — BUILD SUCCESS).

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Relaxed the `telephone` field constraint on the `OwnerFields` schema by removing the `pattern: '^[0-9]*$'`. That pattern would have rejected raw input containing separators (e.g. `(04) 1234-5678`) at request-binding time, before any normalization could run. Kept `minLength`/`maxLength` and documented the new behavior. (This DTO is generated from the spec at build time.)

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — After mapping the incoming fields to an `Owner`, it now strips every non-digit character (`replaceAll("\\D", "")`) and:
   - Returns **400 Bad Request** when the result is not exactly 10 digits.
   - Otherwise stores the normalized 10-digit value, which is then persisted and returned as `telephone`.

**How it satisfies the two acceptance tests:**
- `(04) 1234-5678` → stripped to `0412345678` (10 digits) → stored and returned as `telephone`.
- `12345` → stripped to `12345` (5 digits) → rejected with 400.

The existing `Owner` entity constraint (`@Pattern("^[0-9]{10}$")`) remains satisfied because the controller always writes a normalized 10-digit value before saving, and existing seed/generated data already uses 10-digit numbers.
